dedupe_keys.name: nasctn cbrs sharing ecosystem assessment sea spectrum measurements 3530 to 3710 mhz 2024 to 2026

description: The NASCTN Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) Sharing Ecosystem Assessment measures how well the shared 3.5 GHz band works between commercial users and Department of Defense incumbent systems, such as naval radars, and tracks changes in the spectrum environment over time. Sensor systems were installed at selected sites on the east and west coasts of the United States, with a control and prototyping system in Boulder, Colorado. The data are time- and frequency-selective power measurements from 3530 to 3710 MHz from summer 2024 to summer 2026, recorded with sensors running the IEEE 802.15.22.3 Spectrum Characterization and Occupancy Sensing (SCOS) system and saved in the SigMF signal metadata format. A companion SEA-DATA web portal is listed separately by NIST. Coverage: coastal sensor sites in the United States, 2024 to 2026. Format and access: SigMF files through the NIST public data repository, free under the NIST open licence. Caveats: few sites, chosen near coasts where radars operate; power measurements, not decoded signals; large files. Simulation uses: measured occupancy and interference levels in a shared band for capacity and coexistence studies of 5G and fixed wireless networks. Related records: model-ntia-itm and model-ntia-ehata are the propagation models used in CBRS protection; data-fcc-uls-license-data gives licensed CBRS priority access holders.
